target_paper_title: FLASHVID: EFFICIENT VIDEO LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS VIA TRAINING-FREE TREE-BASED SPA-TIOTEMPORAL TOKEN MERGING

related_work_items.paper_title: Fastvid: Dynamic density pruning for fast video large language models

evidence.evidence_text: We compare FlashVID with four state-of-the-art training-free VLLM acceleration methods ... FastVID, compressing redundant tokens via density-based spatiotemporal pruning.
We test the efficiency of our FlashVID on LLaVA-OneVision, comparing to FastVID.
State-of-the-art VLLM acceleration methods commonly apply video partitioning before token compression, aiming to avoid information mixing and building upon DySeg.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: FastVID is a main direct baseline in the same training-free VLLM acceleration setting and is repeatedly used to frame FlashVID's gains in both effectiveness and efficiency.

related_work_items.paper_title: Prunevid: Visual token pruning for efficient video large language models

evidence.evidence_text: Recent VLLM acceleration methods typically adopt a three-stage pipeline ... however, previous methods typically compress temporal and spatial redundancy independently.
We compare FlashVID with four state-of-the-art training-free VLLM acceleration methods ... PruneVID, combining spatiotemporal token merging with attention-based selection in the LLM.
PruneVID distinguishes static and dynamic tokens, whereas the paper argues for a unified structure-aware mechanism to capture coupled spatiotemporal redundancy.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: PruneVID is a close comparison target because it also addresses efficient video token pruning, but the paper positions FlashVID against its decoupled handling of spatiotemporal redundancy.

related_work_items.paper_title: Visionzip: Longer is better but not necessary in vision language models

evidence.evidence_text: While advances have been achieved in visual token compression for images ... extending these methods to video remains largely underexplored.
VisionZip prunes tokens using [CLS] attention and spatial merging before the LLM.

evidence.section: C.1 REPRODUCTION DETAILS OF COMPARED BASELINES
evidence.evidence_text: VisionZip prunes visual tokens at the output of the vision encoder ... we instead apply pruning after pooling for VisionZip.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: VisionZip is a strong bridge baseline from image/VLM token compression that the paper uses to motivate why video-specific spatiotemporal modeling is needed.

related_work_items.paper_title: An image is worth 1/2 tokens after layer 2: Plug-and-play inference acceleration for large visionlanguage models

evidence.evidence_text: FastV selects prompt-relevant tokens via text-to-visual attention at the prefilling stage.
FastV shows the weakest performance, as early-layer pruning is unstable.
FastV identifies text-relevant visual tokens based on text-to-visual attention in the LLM.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: FastV is a representative earlier token-pruning approach that the paper directly compares against, especially to show the limits of early-layer spatial pruning for video.

related_work_items.paper_title: Holitom: Holistic token merging for fast video large language models

evidence.evidence_text: HoliTom combines global redundancy-aware video partition with spatial and inner-LLM compression.
The paper criticizes previous methods for compressing temporal and spatial redundancy independently and motivates joint spatiotemporal compression.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: HoliTom is part of the immediate lineage of video token compression frameworks that combine multiple compression stages, making it a relevant bridge work for FlashVID's hybrid design.

related_work_items.paper_title: Dycoke: Dynamic compression of tokens for fast video large language models

evidence.evidence_text: DyCoke merges redundant tokens in each segment.
State-of-the-art VLLM acceleration methods commonly apply video partitioning before token compression.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: DyCoke is a nearby video compression method that informs the segmented compression pipeline FlashVID builds on but extends with unified tree-based spatiotemporal merging.

related_work_items.paper_title: Multi-granular spatio-temporal token merging for training-free acceleration of video llms

evidence.evidence_text: The paper argues that decoupled temporal token merging fails to capture video dynamics and may merge less correlated tokens at fixed spatial locations.
Several token compression frameworks for VLLMs have been proposed, including methods that merge or compress spatiotemporal tokens.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: This work is relevant because it also targets training-free spatiotemporal token merging, but FlashVID frames its own contribution around more faithful dynamic spatiotemporal correspondence via redundancy trees.

related_work_items.paper_title: Video instruction tuning with synthetic data

evidence.evidence_text: The paper evaluates on three representative VLLMs, including LLaVA-OneVision.
We evaluate our method on three representative VLLMs: LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video, and Qwen2.5-VL.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: LLaVA-Video is one of the core VLLM backbones used for evaluation, so it is part of the model lineage that FlashVID is designed to accelerate.

evidence.evidence_text: LLaVA-OneVision demonstrates strong video understanding capabilities through task transfer from images.
FlashVID preserves 99.1% of the vanilla model's accuracy even at 10% retention and is evaluated extensively on LLaVA-OneVision.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: LLaVA-OneVision is a central target architecture in the experiments, making it important lineage context for understanding where FlashVID plugs in.

evidence.evidence_text: Qwen2.5-VL uses Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding and is one of the representative VLLMs in the paper.
When integrated into Qwen2.5-VL, FlashVID enables processing of up to 10× more video frames and achieves the largest performance gains under fixed computational budget.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: Qwen2.5-VL is another main evaluation backbone, so it serves as model-lineage context rather than a competing compression method.
